legend: Monotonous cells with low-grade nuclei forming cribriform and glandular spaces line inconspicuous fibrovascular cores.

CK5 staining shows myoepithelial cells present at the periphery of the duct, and demonstrates their absence in the fibrovascular cores, indicative of papillary ductal carcinoma in situ. The absence of expression in the epithelial cells confirms the impression of atypia.

H&E staining reveals two cell populations. One is luminal with apical snouts. The other, with more-abundant pale cytoplasm (called globoid cells), mimics hyperplastic myoepithelium; however, the nuclei are large and atypical, similar to the luminal-type cells.
A panel of myoepithelial immunostains demonstrates the lack of myoepithelium; both cell populations in this image are epithelium (p63 immunostaining is shown here).
A monotonous proliferation of ductal epithelial cells with low nuclear grade lines delicate branching fibrovascular cores within a small cystic duct.

A monotonous proliferation of ductal epithelial cells with low nuclear grade lines delicate branching fibrovascular cores within a small cystic duct. p63 immunostaining shows no evidence of myoepithelium along the fibrovascular cores but highlights the nuclei of the myoepithelial cells surrounding the duct.
A monotonous proliferation of ductal epithelial cells with low nuclear grade lines delicate branching fibrovascular cores.

ADH5 cocktail immunostaining. The neoplastic epithelial cells express luminal cytokeratins (CK7 and CK18: red chromogen) but are negative for basal cytokeratins (CK5, CK14, and nuclear p63: brown chromogen). Myoepithelial cells (brown chromogen) are present around the duct containing the papillary ductal carcinoma in situ, but not along the fibrovascular cores of papillary ductal carcinoma in situ.
The neoplastic cells show strong and diffuse nuclear staining for ER. The palisading arrangement of the neoplastic cells is evident along and around the fibrovascular cores.

Papillary ductal carcinoma in situ showing the presence of low-grade malignant cells forming elaborate papillary structures within dilated ductal spaces. A peripheral layer of myoepithelial cells lining the dilated ductal space can be identified.
Floating proliferation of cancer cells with a micropapillary structure lacking a myoepithelial cell layer and associated with fibrovascular stroma within the ducts.
Papillary ductal carcinoma in situ on core biopsy shows expanded lobules with duct and ductules containing a papillary proliferation of monomorphic columnar cells.
